scope_split.note: `retry` and the four lifecycle commands share `memory:manage`; `reflect` has its own scope so it can be withheld independently of lifecycle management.

response_shape_note: A lifecycle command has two shapes: a fresh transition returns `before`/`after` and a replay does not. A client that assumes one will break on the other.

recorded.statement: `request_retry` and the lifecycle commands refuse any actor that is not human or system with `forbidden_actor_kind` at 403 (the class is `errors.ForbiddenActorKind`); `reflect` requires `memory:reflect`, which key issuance will not grant to an agent. Sources: memory/jobs.py, memory/lifecycle.py, memory/api.py, errors.py.

`reflect` is the only path to the engine's generator and requires an explicit user request; the adapter refuses when `explicit_user_request` is false. A complicated ordinary question goes to recall. It is unreachable from a Context build. Sources: memory/adapter.py, memory/api.py.

A lifecycle command without `expected_revision` is refused with `missing_expected_revision` at 400 (the class is `errors.MissingExpectedRevision`), and a stale one with `revision_conflict` at 409; the state is checked before the revision, so 'you cannot obsolete a tombstone' is answered as `invalid_state_transition` rather than as a stale revision, and an illegal command appends no Event at all. Source: memory/lifecycle.py, errors.py.

A retry may not change the job's `document_id`, `content_sha256` or `bank_id`: those columns are immutable by trigger and the command touches none of them. A `DONE` job is refused rather than retained twice, a `RUNNING` job is refused rather than stolen from its worker, and a `PENDING` job is refused because it is already queued — accepting it would append an audit Event for a transition that did not happen. All three answer `invalid_state_transition` at 409, and only a `FAILED` job is retried, with `retry_count` **reset to 0** rather than incremented. Source: memory/jobs.py, errors.py.

Both the retry and the lifecycle commands are idempotent on `event_id`: a repeat returns the original command Event and writes no second transition. The retry hashes the command payload (excluding `previous_status`/`previous_retry_count`), so the same request re-sent after it already succeeded is recognised as the same command. Source: memory/jobs.py, memory/lifecycle.py.

No write here may change Rule or State, and every reply that describes a memory object says it is not Truth: the four lifecycle commands carry `non_authoritative` and `reflect` carries it too, while a retry reply is only `job`/`event`/`replayed` and names no memory at all — which is why this rule is stated per reply rather than per endpoint. Sources: taskbook §6, memory/api.py.
P4 withholds engine free text from any actor that is not human or system, inside `_respond`, so it applies to every write response too. Source: memory/api.py.
